meta.cite: Barton O. Oliver's mTOR Atlas. doi:10.5281/zenodo.22059963

data.mechanism: Deleting S6K1 extends median lifespan in FEMALE mice (+19% in SEL2009); the effect was not significant in males. A separate study found that S6K1 loss protects against diet-induced obesity (UMX2004, which did not measure lifespan). Read the sex qualifier as part of the claim: this is the clearest evidence that one downstream branch, rather than mTORC1 as a whole, carries much of the ageing signal, and it is also the result whose qualifier is most often dropped in retelling.
data.mechanism_beginner: Removing S6K1 makes FEMALE mice live longer (about a fifth longer) and resist obesity. In male mice the same change did not significantly extend life – that difference is part of the result, not a footnote. Still strong evidence that one branch, not the whole pathway, drives much of the ageing effect.
data.boundary: Female mice only in SEL2009 - the lifespan extension was not significant in males.
data.note: Feeds the sex-dimorphism hypothesis H6 in Knowledge_Gaps. 2026-10-10: UMX2004 no longer cited as support for the lifespan arrow; it measured obesity and insulin sensitivity, not lifespan.
